Real browser on a real TLS --public gateway (throwaway :18443, this worktree's code, default reaper timings): every terminal WS closes code=1006 and the delta SSE errors on an exact ~30s cadence (t+26.8s/57.4s/88.0s), reconnecting… caption flashing each wave — 3 times in a 100s hold — despite 10s pings flowing. Mechanism isolated: https.Server emits 'connection' with the RAW TCP socket but req.socket is the TLSSocket, so the reaper's header deadline armed on the raw socket is never disarmed by 'request'/'upgrade' and destroys every TLS connection at headerMs (30s); plain-HTTP control unaffected (probe: HTTPS SSE reaped at 1513ms with headerMs=1500, HTTP survived).

Re-measured because this change rewrote the line that BUILDS the frame: the full frame's bytes and tag now come from [[graph-cache]]'s one board identity instead of being derived inline here. Run against a throwaway backend on the fixed tree (pinned PORT 8799, live :8787 untouched). Subscriber A anchored on 405 nodes and disconnected, leaving zero delta subscribers; during the gap I created a real spec node through the filesystem surface the project-root watcher owns. B then anchored on 406 nodes CONTAINING the gap-time node, its node-set equal to a concurrent /api/graph poll, on a tag different from A's era tag — a fresh build, not an heirloom. Worth recording how nearly this read false: my first run waited a flat 6s and saw B anchor 405 against a poll of 406, which looks exactly like the defect. It was the probe. Adding a CONTROL that polls during the gap until the board itself absorbs the change showed the board was still at 405 at 2.5s and only reached 406 at 5s — B had simply connected before the build landed, so the anchor was current-at-build-time. A stale-anchor claim is only falsifiable once the board is proven converged BEFORE the new era opens.

Measured against a throwaway backend on the fixed tree (pinned PORT 8799, live :8787 untouched). Subscribed with no position and took a graph-full of 642659B at tag 378402458e38…, disconnected, then — with nobody subscribed — made a real board change through a product action and LEFT it in place. Reconnecting with from=378402458e38… was answered with a graph-delta of 20237B whose from is exactly the position named, carrying the whole offline gap in ONE frame: 7 session units, including the one I changed plus the rows that moved on their own while I was away. That is 3.15% of the snapshot the same reconnect used to cost. Reconnecting with a tag the server has never published (forty zeroes) was answered with a full 642659B snapshot, which is the degradation the design wants — unreachable becomes everything, never a patch computed from a position the server cannot vouch for. Worth recording a first attempt that read falsely PASS: I renamed and renamed BACK before reconnecting, so the board returned to byte-identical content, the tag did not move, and the resume delta was an empty 117B envelope. It proved the plumbing and nothing about carrying a gap. The scenario now requires that the frame's to has actually moved, so an empty patch cannot be mistaken for a resume.
